turns.assessment: No symptom was found in the available data, and all monitored optical metrics on svc265's working route—including receive power, OSNR, pre-FEC BER, DGD, SOP rate, channel power, amplifier powers, and pump currents—remained unchanged. Numerous services sharing the S13–S15, S15–S04, and S04–S14 infrastructure are healthy, strongly arguing against a shared optical-path fault. A service-specific endpoint or unmonitored ODU/client issue remains possible, but the evidence does not identify a cause.

proposals.rationale: An endpoint client-port problem could affect only svc265 without changing line-side optical measurements. However, the documented effect is a hard CLIENT_DOWN condition, not merely degraded quality, and no corroborating symptom was found.

Receiver-local degradation can isolate errors to one receiver while leaving other channels normal. This is weakly supported because every listed line receiver on the working route reported unchanged pre-FEC BER and other quality metrics.

A channel-specific filter shift can reduce signal quality without a power change. It is unlikely because the relevant line-interface OSNR and pre-FEC BER measurements were unchanged and other evidence does not localize a WSS.

score.why: cause flagged as unconsidered and absent
